author: Maya R., RN · fictional practitioner profile
reality: Interruptions, prioritization, bodily care, and emotional handoffs—not a polished recruiting tour.

scenes.title: The handoff is already behind
scenes.prompt: You inherit four patients. One has new confusion, one needs discharge teaching, a family is asking for an update, and a pump is alarming. What do you do first?

choices.label: Assess the newly confused patient
choices.feedback: Strong triage. Acute confusion can signal a time-sensitive change; the alarm still needs delegation.

choices.label: Silence and inspect the pump
choices.feedback: You reduced immediate noise, but delayed assessment of a potentially deteriorating patient.

choices.label: Update the waiting family
choices.feedback: The family feels heard, but clinical urgency has to outrank communication.

scenes.title: A medication does not look right
scenes.prompt: The ordered dose differs from the patient’s home list. The unit is busy and the prescriber is not answering. What next?

choices.label: Hold it and escalate through charge nurse/pharmacy
choices.feedback: Correct safety behavior. It adds friction and documentation—the unglamorous part of the job.

choices.label: Give the ordered dose to stay on schedule
choices.feedback: Schedule pressure never resolves a medication discrepancy.

choices.label: Ask the patient which dose they expect
choices.feedback: Useful context, but not enough to verify an order.

scenes.title: The shift ends, the chart does not
scenes.prompt: You are exhausted. Two routine notes remain and day shift is ready for report. What do you do?

choices.label: Give report, then finish concise factual notes
choices.feedback: A realistic compromise: safe handoff first, then defensible documentation.

choices.label: Finish every detail before handoff
choices.feedback: Thorough, but delays information the next nurse needs now.

choices.label: Leave; the next shift can infer the rest
choices.feedback: Missing documentation shifts risk to colleagues and patients.

author: Luis T., journeyman · fictional practitioner profile
reality: Early mornings, verification, repetitive prep, and asking before guessing.
